```{python}
#| include: false
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd()))
import charts
from charts import raw_html, pct

s = charts.status()
landscape = charts.category_landscape()
share = charts.query("""
    SELECT category_name, SUM(deals) AS deals FROM mart_category_share
    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1
""").iloc[0]
result = charts.query("SELECT result, median_lift FROM mart_lift_by_result WHERE venue = 'home'"
                      ).set_index("result")["median_lift"]
season = charts.query("""
    SELECT c.short_name, s.change_vs_prev, s.season,
           COUNT(*) OVER () AS clubs,
           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.change_vs_prev > 0) OVER () AS up
    FROM mart_attention_by_season AS s JOIN dim_club AS c USING (club_id)
    WHERE s.season = (SELECT MAX(season) FROM mart_attention_by_season)
      AND s.change_vs_prev IS NOT NULL
    ORDER BY s.change_vs_prev DESC LIMIT 1
""").iloc[0]
n_tests = len(list((Path.cwd().parent / "tests").glob("test_*.sql")))
tests = charts.sponsor_match_day_tests()
higher = int((tests["group"] == "Reliably higher").sum())
top_lift = charts.query("""
    SELECT c.short_name, l.median_lift, l.season FROM mart_club_match_lift AS l
    JOIN dim_club AS c USING (club_id)
    WHERE l.season = (SELECT MAX(season) FROM mart_club_match_lift)
    ORDER BY l.median_lift DESC LIMIT 1
""").iloc[0]
stadium = charts.query("""
    SELECT SUM(deals) FILTER (WHERE sold_by = 'stadium_owner') AS venue_sold,
           SUM(deals) AS total
    FROM mart_stadium_naming_by_seller
""").iloc[0]
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(raw_html(f"""
<section class="hero">
  <div class="eyebrow">Sponsorship research · Public-attention data</div>
  <h1>Who sponsors MLS, and who's paying attention?</h1>
  <p>Every front-of-kit, sleeve and stadium naming partner across all {int(s.clubs_total)} MLS clubs,
  each with a cited source, joined to daily Wikipedia attention for every club and sponsor brand
  and {int(s.club_match_days):,} club match days.</p>
  <div class="hero-actions">
    <a class="btn-solid" href="sponsors.html">Explore the sponsors</a>
    <a class="btn-ghost" href="attention.html">See match-day attention</a>
  </div>
  <div class="live">Rebuilt daily · pageviews through {charts.show_date(s.pageviews_through)}</div>
</section>
"""))
print(raw_html(charts.kpi_row([
    (f"{int(s.current_deals)}", "Current deals", f"{int(s.brands)} sponsor brands"),
    (f"{int(s.clubs_covered)}/{int(s.clubs_total)}", "Clubs covered", "front of kit, sleeve, stadium"),
    (f"{s.rows_sourced / s.rows_total:.0%}", "Rows with a source", f"last checked {charts.show_date(s.last_checked)}"),
    (f"{int(s.club_match_days):,}", "Club match days", f"pageviews since {s.pageviews_from:%Y}"),
])))
```

## What the data says

print(raw_html(f"""

    <div class="f-link">Venue ownership →</div></a>

"""))

## How it works

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(raw_html(f"""
<div class="pipeline">
  <div><strong>Hand-sourced dataset</strong>Every deal is a CSV row with a source URL and the date it was checked.</div>
  <div><strong>Daily ingestion</strong>Wikipedia pageviews (Wikimedia API) and MLS results (American Soccer Analysis), incremental and idempotent.</div>
  <div><strong>DuckDB warehouse</strong>A type 2 deal history, a 28-day attention baseline and match-day lift, built in SQL.</div>
  <div><strong>Tested every run</strong>{n_tests} SQL data tests gate the publish. A failed test keeps yesterday's page up.</div>
  <div><strong>Published here</strong>GitHub Actions renders this site every morning.</div>
</div>
"""))
```

Pageviews measure **public attention**, not sponsorship value, reach or return.
See [Methods](methods.qmd) for how each number is built and where it falls short.
